title: Completed constant coefficients on a small site at independent universes
statement: Let $C$ be a small category in universe $c$, with Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $A$ be a commutative ring in an independent universe $a$, with a specified element $p\in A$. Fix an enlargement universe $w$ and work with commutative ring sheaves valued in $\max(a,c,w)$. Write $\underline T$ for the constant ring sheaf, namely the sheafification of the constant presheaf on the universe lift of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For $n\in\mathbf N$ define $A_n=A/(p)^{n+1}$ and $q_n:A\to A_n$ to be the quotient map. The transition $t_n:\underline{A_{n+1}}\to\underline{A_n}$ is constant sheafification of the quotient factor map induced by the identity of $A$. Define the inverse sequence $T:\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Sh(C,J;\mathrm{CRing})$ with objects $\underline{A_n}$ and consecutive maps $t_n$, and define $B=\varprojlim T$ with its limit projections [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. The sheafified quotient maps obey $t_n\underline{q_{n+1}}=\underline{q_n}$ and form a cone. Define $\iota:\underline A\to B$ as the limit lift of that cone. For $U\in C$, let $\eta_U:A\to\underline A(U)$ be the constant-presheaf sheafification unit (with the universe lift understood); define $s_U=\iota_U(\eta_U(p))$. Naturality of the unit and of $\iota$ gives $B(f)(s_U)=s_V$ for every $f:V\to U$, so $s=(s_U)_U$ is a global section. These definitions impose no nonzero, regularity or uniformizer hypothesis on $p$. Their application to valuation rings with a specified uniformizer supplies the small-site, independently enlarged presentation of the completed coefficients; the existing scheme-specific completed-coefficients interface [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] is retained unchanged.

proof.text: For quotient_compatible, simplify the constant functor map and the consecutive map of Functor.ofOpSequence. Unfold the quotient and transition and use functoriality to combine their images under constant sheafification. The two input ring morphisms are definitionally equal: the factor map sends the class of every a at exponent n+2 to its class at exponent n+1, and ULift preserves this formula. This proves the cone equation without any assumption on p.

For uniformizer_natural, compose the constant-presheaf sheafification unit with the underlying natural transformation of constantMap. Evaluate its naturality square at ULift.up p. The constant presheaf restriction is the identity, so the resulting equality, reversed, is exactly the claimed restriction equation for the completed sections. This applies to every morphism of the site, including the vacuous empty-site case.
